:::note[About this page]
This page is an unofficial guide to S1000D® Issue 7, written in this project's own words. It is based on the S1000D distribution dated 2026-07-16. This is a personal project and is not affiliated with ASD ([Specification files and trademarks](/s1000d-stack/guide/license/)). The formal definition is in Chap 3.9.5.1, Chap 3.9.6.1 (Table 64) of the S1000D specification and in the [S1000D Issue 7 data dictionary](https://users.s1000d.org/S1000D_DD_7/Files/attributes/securityClassification.xml).
:::

`securityClassification` is the attribute that gives the security classification. The security classification of a whole data module is written on the `security` element of the identification and status section. Elements of the content can carry it too.

## Elements that carry it

In the 33 XML schemas of Issue 7, 567 elements carry this attribute. The following table shows the 12 elements that appear in the most schemas.

| Element | Schemas | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `acronym` | 28 | Optional |
| `acronymDefinition` | 28 | Optional |
| `attentionListItemPara` | 28 | Optional |
| `attentionRandomList` | 28 | Optional |
| `attentionRandomListItem` | 28 | Optional |
| `attentionSequentialList` | 28 | Optional |
| `attentionSequentialListItem` | 28 | Optional |
| `changeInline` | 28 | Optional |
| `circuitBreakerRef` | 28 | Optional |
| `controlAuthority` | 28 | Optional |
| `controlAuthorityGroup` | 28 | Optional |
| `copyright` | 28 | Optional |

## Allowed values

The allowed values are decided in two steps: by the XML schema and by BREX (Business Rules Exchange).

| Defined by | Content |
| --- | --- |
| XML schema | The type is `securityClassificationAttType` (based on `xs:string`). The values are an enumeration of 99 values, from `01` to `99` |
| Default BREX (BREX-S1-00231) | Allows 10 values (including ranges and patterns) for `//@securityClassification`. The rule applies to all schemas |

Of the values in the XML schema enumeration, the 41 values `10` to `50` are not allowed by BREX-S1-00231. They pass XML schema validation, but they are violations in a check against the default BREX.

BREX-S1-00231 allows the following values and defines how a lower-level BREX can tailor each of them.

| Value | `valueForm` | `valueTailoring` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `01` to `09` | `single` | `closed` |
| `51~99` | `range` | `restrictable` |

## Meaning of the values

The project defines the meaning of the values. The default BREX allows `01` to `09` and the range `51~99`, but it does not give their meaning. The data dictionary does not give it either. Check the business rules of the project to find which value stands for which classification.

## In this stack

| Operation | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| Read | [`read_data_module`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/reader/read-data-module/). The value is in the identification and status section (`identAndStatus`) |
| Write it when a data module is created | `draft.securityClassification` of [`build_data_module`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/writer/build-data-module/). It cannot be omitted. The tool does not fill in a value; it writes the value as given |
| Look up the values and their meaning | [`lookup_value`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/brex/lookup-value/). If the project BREX gives the meaning of a value, the tool returns it |

For a value whose meaning the project BREX does not give either, no tool can return a meaning.
